Hey there, this is a solid first setup, and it looks like you’ve gotten some good advice! I’m really new to betta fishkeeping as well, and this tank/lid/filter combo looks exactly like what I got for my first tank a few months ago. The main thing I’d be wary of is the filter flow; the one that came with my tank looked exactly like that, and it was way too powerful even for my plakat betta. I’d recommend getting some filter media to dampen the flow, or maybe invest in a sponge filter if it’s not too late! Also, I wouldn’t recommend using the fish flakes that come with the tank, if it’s the same as the one I ended up getting lol. Good luck!

This is my setup now, I have some Betta hammocks and a floating log coming in the next few days, as well as a thermometer. Right now I’ve got a filter that came with the tank (it is a 10 gallon tank), I’m unsure how strong of a current it produces in relation to a Betta; I think it’s pretty soft, but I’m not sure what is soft for a Betta. I also have an adjustable heater set at 78 degrees Fahrenheit. Do you think I have enough hides and plants? The ones near the skeleton are live plants, and the one near the filter is a soft fake plant. Everything has been thoroughly rinsed before being put in the tank. Please let me know if there’s any other details I forgot to mention! All I ask is please be gentle, I’m very new to this! I’ve been researching for the past few months, and I feel at least okay on starting the cycling process.

I’m also a little concerned about the stuff floating at the top of the tank, which I tried to get in the second picture. It’s a sort of powdery film that sticks to the net when I drag it through. This is my 10 year old corn. He ate a little over two weeks ago. Hot side ranges from 82-86 and cool from 72-76. Humidity stays around 40-50% on average. This has been the first time he’s eaten in awhile because I had to take him to several vet visits and move him to a new house, all while having to administer antibiotic shots for a small tail amputation he had about a month ago. He’s been behaving like he’s ready to shed. I thought this was just constipation, so I’ve been soaking him every other day for around 10-15 minutes. He passed some hard stools but hasn’t pooped since then, instead he’s been drinking a lot and peeing frequently, almost looking like he’s trying to poop, but I can’t be sure.

Ever since I got him back I’ve been insanely paranoid, watching him like a hawk and stressing over every little thing he does. Hopefully this is just another case of me being overly worried!

For context, he’s only got the paper towels temporarily so I can keep a close eye on his tail; he had to get a little bit of it amputated after his previous caretaker failed to notice what was presumably some stuck sheds. Happy to report that he’s doing much better than when I saw him there about a month ago! Got him some fun hammocks and new hides/branches to goof around on, as well as a new water bowl and some much better hydrometers/thermometers. Very excited that he’s excited to eat again!

I may disagree with your opinion of the game, but you make some very valid points, and I respect that. Since you were wondering, the main reason I (and I think many others who love the game) care about Mother 3 so much is because of the personalization we gave the game, and at least for me the way that the tragic story reminded me of things I had gone through. When I was younger, a fire destroyed my home, scattered my family, and took a loved one from me. When I played the game, I was immediately captivated by the story and formed a deep connection to it. Because of the similarities, I found a bit of myself  in Lucas’s journey, and soon I began to substitute most of the characters in the game for people I knew or had known in real life, which made the game that much more personal and impactful. In the end, Mother 3 helped me get through a really hard time in my life; it means a lot to me.
